page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 2880 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core metrics. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth tests fall into the bottom 25%, though large-block write operations maintain average performance. Text processing is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25%, while database operations and static web serving throughput are weaker, landing in the bottom 25%.

The L4aos_v4 offers a high-density local storage profile combined with a generous memory allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial local data caching without the overhead of external storage. However, the weak memory read bandwidth and lower multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive parallel computing. This server is best suited for workloads such as local database caching, text processing, lightweight Redis deployments, and general-purpose tasks that benefit from fast single-core execution and high local storage capacity rather than high-throughput memory operations.
